# **General Game Notes**

- Timing begins on the first frame of player movement or pausing in Link's house, whichever comes first. Other inputs will not start the timer. For example, you may change the camera with C-Up if you wish. The player is also required to begin the run within 10s of gaining control.
- If defeating Ganon, timing ends on the first frame of the final blow cutscene.
- If wrong warping into the credits, timing ends on the first frame of the fade-in of any cutscene which normally takes place after the Ganon final slash, and which will eventually reach The End screen (i.e. no void loops).
- Any method of starting a run which causes your first pause to begin anywhere other than the Map subscreen is banned. This includes reaching file select from a "no save, no continue". 
Note: PAL starts on the Item Subscreen normally, so it is exempt from this rule.

## **Intro Skip**

- Skipping the intro cutscene is allowed (but not mandatory). To do this, watch the intro once, then save the game in Link's house. You may wish to put this prepared file into slot 2 or 3. Then any time you wish to do a speedrun attempt, you can copy the prepared file into slot 1, and do your run there. 
- Skipping the intro will cause you to lose approximately four frames due to a starting position that is further from the door in Link's house. 
- Getting the rupee from the pot in Link's house is BANNED when first loading an intro skip file.

## **Console menu specific rules**

- Console specific menus (like the VC menu) may not be used for unintended purposes (e.g. you can't use them for pause buffering).
- The use of restore points (savestates) is banned.
- The use of suspend points (launching the game from where you quit) is allowed.

## **N64-specific rules**

- Crooked Cartridge is not allowed.
- Runs done on Everdrive or any flash cart equivalent are not allowed.

## **VC-specific rules**

- As of February 15th 2018, you must use an official version of IOS 9. Runs with Wiis that have a reset duration faster than 13 seconds are not allowed. 
Check the IOS 9 video linked in the resources section for more info.
- 1.0/1.1 injects are banned.

## **GC-specific rules**

- You must use an official GameCube disc. Emulators, ISO Loaders and burnt discs are not allowed.
- Using an unofficial MIOS is not allowed.

## **Emulator-specific rules**

- Emulator is banned for all times that are within 10% of the existing record. You can look up what the current cutoffs are on [this website](https://oot-emu-cutoffs.scaramangado.de).

### *N64 Emulation*

- You must use Project64 1.6 or 1.7. All other emulators and versions (such as Mupen64/Bizhawk/Project64 2.0+) are banned.
- You must use the default settings for emulation (e.g. Changing the graphics plugin to do GIM is not allowed).

### *Wii Emulation*

- You must use a Dolphin version at or newer than 5.0-15999 (ideally you just set dolphin to auto-update, should this version range change, we will make an announcement). 
- "Emulated CPU Clock Override" may be set up to 115% to fix Dolphin-specific slowdowns to feel more on-par with hardware (recommended).
- "Store EFB Copies to Texture Only" may be unchecked to fix the pause screen (recommended).
- "Enable Dual Core" may be checked (recommended).
- "Enable Cheats" must be unchecked.
- Any graphics backend is allowed.
- Internal Resolution must be "Native", Anti-Aliasing: "None", Anisotropic Filtering: "1x" .
- All other GFX- and CPU-modifying settings must be set to their defaults.

## **Controller and Controller Adapter rules**

- Analog signals can only be mapped to analog forms of input (eg. mapping movement to a button is not allowed).
- Digital signals can be mapped to analog inputs (eg. mapping C-Buttons on the C-Stick is allowed).
- The control stick output must be a monotonically increasing sequence. In other words, if one input value is greater than or equal to another input value, their respective outputs must share that relationship. This preserves the ordering of deadzone → ESS → walking → running.
- Minimum input must be mapped to minimum output. In other words, neutral must map to neutral. Note that this rule only applies to adapter remappings. Using your controller's neutral-reset functionality is legal.
- The adapter may not add functionality to the game. Turbo, macros, and mapping multiple input sources to movement are examples of added functionality.
- Adapters and input displays are not allowed to give you more information than looking at an unmodified controller (so no exact values, ess range indicators, etc).
- Throughout the duration of any speedrun, you are only allowed to use one controller with one analog mapping for each of the 4 input streams that OoT can receive. In other words, you may not switch controllers, switch mappings, change calibration, or toggle on/off calibration or mappings during your run. Whatever controllers+mappings+calibrations you begin the run with is what you are bound to use for the duration of the run.

## **Video rules**

As of September 10th 2017, all submissions require video. In addition, as of December 5th 2019, videos should conform to the following guidelines:

- The video has to be permanent. YouTube videos are preferred, but if you really want to use something else, make sure the video stays up. Twitch vods or highlights are *not* allowed.
- The full run has to be shown in the video (from before file select until after when timing ends, no parts missing).
- For timing purposes, no frame drops may occur at the start and end of the run.
- The video has to be one single recording (no splices, no separate videos).
- The video feed has to be of acceptable quality.
- The game audio has to be clearly audible throughout the whole run and has to be of acceptable quality. Stream notifications and such are ok, but no music playing through the run for extended durations.

categories.rules:
# Individual Level rules

- The start of the run should be the first time the dungeon has been entered, aside from exceptions for clearing opening cutscenes.
- Starting from file select is allowed.
- Timing starts upon gaining control of Link in the main entrance room of the dungeon (like after a savewarp). [This document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Rlos5ZCZH-EapkamZSq-nH_Y_17YpRUpZlDA6Wpi16I/) lists common cues for identifying the start and ending frames when retiming your run.
- Timing ends:
- Main dungeons: upon losing control of Link when he steps into the blue warp.
- Mini-dungeons: when Link holds the main mini-dungeon item above his head.
- Any platform and/or region is allowed, as long as it follows the general game rules (see 'Game Rules' for more information). Exceptions on the game rules:
    - Using the Practice ROM is allowed, see below.
    - Using Everdrive is allowed.
    - There is no 10% rule for emulators.
- Arbitrary Code Execution is banned and can't be used to set up the file.

# Practice ROM-specific rules

- Savestates, memfiles, warps, inventory editing, and any other functions may be used to set up your file and to reset between attempts.
- The state of the file before the run should conform to what is allowed/possible for the run, meaning that the relevant parts of the file could have been set up manually without Practice ROM functionality.
- During actual IL gameplay, no Practice ROM functionality may be used. For example, no cheats, no visible menus or displays, of course no macros, etc.
- To prove you are not playing a macro, you must pause the game with frame advance either just before or after your attempt, and the pause icon must be visible. Any Practice ROM attempt that does not do this will not be accepted.

# Any% rules

- For the main dungeons, the boss has to be defeated.
- ACE and SRM are banned.
- No further restrictions (apart from mentioned rules above).

# Individual Level rules

* The start of the run should be the first time the dungeon has been entered, aside from exceptions for clearing opening cutscenes.
* Starting from file select is allowed.
* Timing starts upon gaining control of Link in the main entrance room of the dungeon (like after a savewarp). [This document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Rlos5ZCZH-EapkamZSq-nH_Y_17YpRUpZlDA6Wpi16I/) lists common cues for identifying the start and ending frames when retiming your run.

    * Using the Practice ROM is allowed, see below.
    * Using Everdrive is allowed.
    * There is no 10% rule for emulators.
* Arbitrary Code Execution is banned and can't be used to set up the file.
 
# Practice ROM-specific rules
* Savestates, memfiles, warps, inventory editing, and any other functions may be used to set up your file and to reset between attempts.
* The state of the file before the run should conform to what is allowed/possible for the run, meaning that the relevant parts of the file could have been set up manually without Practice ROM functionality.
* During actual IL gameplay, no Practice ROM functionality may be used. For example, no cheats, no visible menus or displays, of course no macros, etc.
* To prove you are not playing a macro, you must pause the game with frame advance either just before or after your attempt, and the pause icon must be visible. Any Practice ROM attempt that does not do this will not be accepted.
 
# 100% Rules
* All chests in the dungeon must be opened (none left on map subscreen).
* All dungeon rooms must be entered (all rooms blue on the map subscreen).
* All Gold Skulltulas in the dungeon must be collected (the Skulltula icon has to appear on the map subscreen).
* For the main dungeons, the boss has to be defeated.
* The Heart Container from the boss must be collected.
* All the goals for 100% must be accomplished manually, and not by setting flags remotely.

# **Ganondorf Source Requirement rules**

## Goal

Defeat Ganon after completing the following objectives:

- Defeat Ganondorf
- Get light arrows
- Collect Shadow and Spirit medallions
- Get magic
- Get Zelda's Lullaby
- Get the Quiver 30

## **Rules and restrictions**

- No wrong warping
- No RBA
- No BA
- No GIM
- No Carry-SRM
- No cutscene skips from blue warps
- Source requirement is enforced for all acquired items. This means all items, equipment, songs, etc. collected in the run must come from one of their natural sources in the game.

Arbitrary Code Execution is banned.
In the context of OoT rules, ACE is defined as:

- Executing code outside of the .text section of a file
- Executing modified code in the .text section of a file 

If code is indirectly modified by some SRM application but it does not benefit the speedrun, it is allowed

**Glitchless All Main Quests Rules**

* Saving and resetting to change Link's position (savewarping) is allowed  
* Dying and continuing to change Link's position (deathwarping) is allowed  
* Timing ends on the first frame of the final blow cutscene

**Clarification:**  
Since there is such a gray area in defining what is or is not a "glitch" in this game, a group of OoT players voted to define a set of rules that they would all abide by. It is important that all players use the same rules, since it allows them to compare times with each other. These rules are not perfect, but they are the current standard. This category aims to create a speedrunning experience which feels like a glitchless category. This is accomplished by requiring intermediate goals in addition to simply beating the game, and by allowing a narrower set of techniques than Glitchless Any%.

**Goal: Complete all of the following main story quests and their prerequisites as the intended age**:

games.rules:
# **General Game Notes**

- Timing begins on the first frame of player movement or pausing in Link's house, whichever comes first. Other inputs will not start the timer. For example, you may change the camera with C-Up if you wish. The player is also required to begin the run within 10s of gaining control.
- If defeating Ganon, timing ends on the first frame of the final blow cutscene.
- If wrong warping into the credits, timing ends on the first frame of the fade-in of any cutscene which normally takes place after the Ganon final slash, and which will eventually reach The End screen (i.e. no void loops).
- Any method of starting a run which causes your first pause to begin anywhere other than the Map subscreen is banned. This includes reaching file select from a "no save, no continue". 
Note: PAL starts on the Item Subscreen normally, so it is exempt from this rule.

## **Intro Skip**

- Skipping the intro cutscene is allowed (but not mandatory). To do this, watch the intro once, then save the game in Link's house. You may wish to put this prepared file into slot 2 or 3. Then any time you wish to do a speedrun attempt, you can copy the prepared file into slot 1, and do your run there. 
- Skipping the intro will cause you to lose approximately four frames due to a starting position that is further from the door in Link's house. 
- Getting the rupee from the pot in Link's house is BANNED when first loading an intro skip file.

## **Console menu specific rules**

- Console specific menus (like the VC menu) may not be used for unintended purposes (e.g. you can't use them for pause buffering).
- The use of restore points (savestates) is banned.
- The use of suspend points (launching the game from where you quit) is allowed.

## **N64-specific rules**

- Crooked Cartridge is not allowed.
- Runs done on Everdrive or any flash cart equivalent are not allowed.

## **VC-specific rules**

- As of February 15th 2018, you must use an official version of IOS 9. Runs with Wiis that have a reset duration faster than 13 seconds are not allowed. 
Check the IOS 9 video linked in the resources section for more info.
- 1.0/1.1 injects are banned.

## **GC-specific rules**

- You must use an official GameCube disc. Emulators, ISO Loaders and burnt discs are not allowed.
- Using an unofficial MIOS is not allowed.

## **Emulator-specific rules**

- Emulator is banned for all times that are within 10% of the existing record. You can look up what the current cutoffs are on [this website](https://oot-emu-cutoffs.scaramangado.de).

### *N64 Emulation*

- You must use Project64 1.6 or 1.7. All other emulators and versions (such as Mupen64/Bizhawk/Project64 2.0+) are banned.
- You must use the default settings for emulation (e.g. Changing the graphics plugin to do GIM is not allowed).

### *Wii Emulation*

- You must use a Dolphin version at or newer than 5.0-15999 (ideally you just set dolphin to auto-update, should this version range change, we will make an announcement). 
- "Emulated CPU Clock Override" may be set up to 115% to fix Dolphin-specific slowdowns to feel more on-par with hardware (recommended).
- "Store EFB Copies to Texture Only" may be unchecked to fix the pause screen (recommended).
- "Enable Dual Core" may be checked (recommended).
- "Enable Cheats" must be unchecked.
- Any graphics backend is allowed.
- Internal Resolution must be "Native", Anti-Aliasing: "None", Anisotropic Filtering: "1x" .
- All other GFX- and CPU-modifying settings must be set to their defaults.

## **Controller and Controller Adapter rules**

- Analog signals can only be mapped to analog forms of input (eg. mapping movement to a button is not allowed).
- Digital signals can be mapped to analog inputs (eg. mapping C-Buttons on the C-Stick is allowed).
- The control stick output must be a monotonically increasing sequence. In other words, if one input value is greater than or equal to another input value, their respective outputs must share that relationship. This preserves the ordering of deadzone → ESS → walking → running.
- Minimum input must be mapped to minimum output. In other words, neutral must map to neutral. Note that this rule only applies to adapter remappings. Using your controller's neutral-reset functionality is legal.
- The adapter may not add functionality to the game. Turbo, macros, and mapping multiple input sources to movement are examples of added functionality.
- Adapters and input displays are not allowed to give you more information than looking at an unmodified controller (so no exact values, ess range indicators, etc).
- Throughout the duration of any speedrun, you are only allowed to use one controller with one analog mapping for each of the 4 input streams that OoT can receive. In other words, you may not switch controllers, switch mappings, change calibration, or toggle on/off calibration or mappings during your run. Whatever controllers+mappings+calibrations you begin the run with is what you are bound to use for the duration of the run.

## **Video rules**

As of September 10th 2017, all submissions require video. In addition, as of December 5th 2019, videos should conform to the following guidelines:

- The video has to be permanent. YouTube videos are preferred, but if you really want to use something else, make sure the video stays up. Twitch vods or highlights are *not* allowed.
- The full run has to be shown in the video (from before file select until after when timing ends, no parts missing).
- For timing purposes, no frame drops may occur at the start and end of the run.
- The video has to be one single recording (no splices, no separate videos).
- The video feed has to be of acceptable quality.
- The game audio has to be clearly audible throughout the whole run and has to be of acceptable quality. Stream notifications and such are ok, but no music playing through the run for extended durations.

**Glitchless Any% rules**

* Saving and resetting to change Link's position (savewarping) is allowed  
* Dying and continuing to change Link's position (deathwarping) is allowed  
* Timing ends on the first frame of the final blow cutscene

**Clarification:**  
Since there is such a gray area in defining what is or is not a "glitch" in this game, a group of OoT players voted to define a set of rules that they would all abide by. It is important that all players use the same rules, since it allows them to compare times with each other. These rules are not perfect, but they are the current standard. This category aims to ban things solely based on the techniques used, not the results of those techniques. To the extent that common sense allows, we may explain this as: "If the means are not a glitch, neither are the ends." So if you do not perform a glitch, you may skip any part of the game, regardless of how important. This category was originally the only Glitchless category. It now stands apart from Glitchless All Main Quests which aims to create a speedrun which feels more like a glitchless category, rather than aiming to be strictly logically glitchless like this one.

**Allowed Techniques:**  
* Power Crouch Stabbing
* Roll invincibility
* Post-damage invincibility
* Jumpslashing in mid-air for more distance
* Shield dropping
* Using broken deku stick
* Hookshot Extension
* Rolling from the blue switch in Jabu Jabu's Belly
* Damage boosting
* Damage Buffering
* Placing bombs on lava pits to damage Volvagia
* Skipping text triggers via weapon swapping
* Passing through the back side of a one-sided collision (e.g. bridge clip, darunia's door, forest's falling ceiling)
* Attacking to collect or hit an object on the other side of a collision
* Momentary Antigravity (e.g. b1 skip)
* Shielding damage midair to take Link out of a backflip or sidehop and into a normal airborne state. A.K.A. "Recoil Jump"
* Twisted sidehops or backflips out of siderolls or standing ESS shuffles
* Touching misplaced or accidentally-exposed loading zones (e.g. Early Jabu and Trials Skip)
* Delaying a timer by pressing cutscene items midair. This includes internal timers such as those used for switches.
* Going Out of Bounds (any area which is beyond the boundary walls of the map, or any area which is exposed to the lowest void plane in the map.)
* Being in an unloaded area
* Hoverboost (equipping hover boots whenever you want, including high speed situations)
* Remote Wall Interactions (touching a wall to interact with another wall sooner, e.g. jump to Volvagia)
* Swimming laterally while wearing Iron Boots.
* Climbing ladders or vines during cutscenes.
* Cutscene skips which only use movement from inputs completed before the cutscene begins (e.g. voiding, entering a loading zone)
*  Using culling for any purpose other than to temporarily halt the normal behavior of an actor with which Link is not currently interacting (such as Schrödinger's Chains)
 
**Banned Techniques:**  
* Infinite Sword Glitch
* Megaflip and megasidehop
* Extended Antigravity (e.g. unloading lower gerudo fortress)
* Ground jump
* All forms of superslide
* Hovering
* Entrance point glitch (or other respawn point manipulation)
* Clipping (note that this is well defined for both solid collision and soft/actor collision. contact a moderator if you aren't sure if something is a clip).
* Cutscene diving to sink into water
* Flame storage
* Item Manipulation (BA, RBA, GIM)
* Using collection delay to your advantage (e.g. early eyeball frog or gold scale. Delay happens naturally in many shops if you buy quickly, this is ok)
* Something except for a sword on B (excluding normal circumstances like riding Epona)
* Bottle Duplication
* Wrong warp
* Void warp
* Walking While Talking
* Causing a switch to remain pressed longer than it should
* Ocarina Items
* Z-slide
* A-slide
* Using restricted items (such as farore's wind in the overworld or ocarina in boss rooms)
* Unloading an actor which clearly should be loaded (e.g. actor glitch, unloading KZ's ice, overloading the graveyard or trials to remove graves or Gold Gauntlet monoliths)
* Abusing actors which have not had a chance to update after loading (such as 0,0,0 glitch and the deku b2 web)
* Opening underwater chests while wearing the Iron Boots
* Dying to achieve anything other than a deathwarp
* Stale Reference Manipulation
* Arbitrary Code Execution
* Quick Putaway

# Goals

- All goal items must be obtained from their natural source at some point during the run

- Maps, Compasses, and Boss Keys are not required
- Ganon's Castle trials are not required
- Scarecrow's song is not required
- The extra Heart Pieces are not required (37th, 38th and 39th HP) and they cannot be substituted for any of the main 36 pieces
- Obtaining the cow in Link's house is not required
- Buying or planting all Magic Beans is not required, only the Magic Bean item in the pause menu is required.
- Duping a bottle over an item is allowed, but your final inventory must be complete
- Gold Skulltula token duping is allowed, but all 100 unique tokens must be collected from their source, and the map icons must be present
- Only the highest upgrades are required for multi-tiered items
- It does not matter what mask is in your inventory at the end of the run, however you must have received the Mask of Truth from the Happy Mask Shop at least once
- Bottle RBA is allowed but you must obtain 4 bottles from their source

- Executing code outside of the .text section of a file
- Executing modified code in the .text section of a file 

*If code is indirectly modified by some SRM application but it does not benefit the speedrun, it is allowed.
